transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Rodriguez (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Helion - CISO), Jordan Lee (Helion - Security Engineer), Priya Nair (Helion - Cloud Ops Manager)

Summary:
Brief security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment models. Main customer concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SSO flows, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS integration, data residency and retention policies. Agreed to follow up with docs and a technical deep-dive/benchmark for dedicated capacity.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Sanjay our solutions engineer, and I think we have Alex, Jordan, and Priya from Helion?
[00:00:12] Alex: Yep, Alex here. Thanks for making time. Just to be clear, we run a lot of regulated workloads so security is, like, our gating factor.
[00:00:20] Maya: Totally understood. The goal today is a quick posture overview and to call out where we need to dig deeper, so we can get you the right artifacts.
[00:00:30] Sanjay: Quick intro from my side: I focus on infra and ops — we'll cover VPC/private deployment, KMS integration, audit logs, and RBAC.
[00:00:38] Priya: Great. Our immediate question is if hosted is acceptable or we need private deployment — depends on encryption at rest and key management, plus auditability.
[00:00:47] Jordan: Also want specifics on SSO/SAML flows and how role mapping works, and whether we get per-request audit logs with token-level info.
[00:00:55] Maya: Got it. At a high level, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem). We can run in your VPC and integrate with customer-managed KMS for private. For hosted, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts we can share.
[00:01:10] Alex: When you say integrate with customer-managed KMS, is that using an HSM or cloud KMS? We need HSM-backed keys for certain data sets.
[00:01:20] Sanjay: We support cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with customer-controlled keys. HSM integration is available via partner KMS in private deployments — we can detail the flow. Sometimes the transcription will say K M S as K-M-S or K-V cache as K-V cash, so forgive the auto-cap.
[00:01:40] Priya: Ok. For retention — how granular are logs? We need immutable audit logs for 12 months, and exportability to our SIEM.
[00:01:49] Sanjay: We emit request-level logs, per token metadata in Dedicated/Private, and we can stream audit logs to your S3 or to a syslog endpoint; retention policies are configurable in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has default retention — but we can arrange longer retention as an add-on.
[00:02:05] Jordan: You mentioned per-token metadata — does that include prompt/response payloads? We have PHI constraints.
[00:02:12] Maya: By default, hosted captures telemetry for debugging but we offer options: redact, not persist, or route logs to customer-managed storage for Private/Dedicated. For PHI, we recommend Private with customer-managed keys and no host-persistent storage.
[00:02:28] Alex: And SOC2 — do you have Type II? Any gaps?
[00:02:32] Maya: Yes, SOC 2 Type II. We'll send the report. For ISO 27001 we have a cert snapshot — will include that too. I'll also include our penetration test summary and SSP.
[00:02:44] Alex: Great. On SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and have strict SCIM provisioning needs. Can you do SCIM for user sync and SAML for auth?
[00:02:53] Sanjay: We support SAML-based SSO and SCIM for provisioning in the Console. For Private deployments, that's straight-forward. For Hosted, we support SAML SSO and can map SAML attributes to RBAC roles — we have a sample mapping we can share.
[00:03:06] Priya: How do you handle multi-tenant RBAC — can we scope datasets per team and ensure strict isolation?
[00:03:12] Sanjay: Yes, RBAC is policy-based. We can define per-tenant roles and enforce per-namespace isolation. On Dedicated we can optionally partition capacity and have network-level isolation.
[00:03:22] Jordan: Any known drift in logs or missing fields when you do continuous batching or KV cache? We need reliable replayability.
[00:03:30] Sanjay: Good callout — continuous batching can change how requests are handled under the hood, but audit logs preserve request boundaries and we surface latency/cost attribution per request. KV cache is the K-V cache, apologies if the auto-transcript renders it odd; the cache keys don't include PII by design.
[00:03:48] Maya: For our compliance pipeline — we can do a security questionnaire or a spreadsheet of answers. Alex, do you have an auditor-provided questionnaire or do you want our standard security pack?
[00:03:58] Alex: We have a vendor security questionnaire (SSQ) that's fairly long — we can share it; would you prefer we drop it into your portal or email?
[00:04:06] Maya: Email works; we'll centralize responses and highlight any required proof.
[00:04:10] Alex: On encryption in transit, do you support TLS 1.3 and mutual TLS for some endpoints?
[00:04:16] Sanjay: Yes, TLS 1.3 across managed endpoints. For Private we can enable mTLS for internal service-to-service calls and customers can require mTLS on ingress gates.
[00:04:26] Priya: For data residency — we need processing within EU for some workloads. Can you pin region and ensure data stays in-region?
[00:04:33] Maya: Yes, we support region pinning and can restrict routing to specific zones. For private deployments, it's customer-run infrastructure so residency is in your control. Hosted can be run in cloud regions with data residency controls and contractual clauses.
[00:04:46] Jordan: How about vulnerability management and patching cadence? We need quarterly evidence and CVE disclosures.
[00:04:52] Sanjay: We do regular patch cycles, CVE tracking, and will provide a summary for SOC2/ISO artifacts. We also provide notification SLAs for critical issues.
[00:05:02] Alex: One more thing — for the Dedicated model, is there a burst or fallback to hosted if capacity is exhausted? We need resilience strategies.
[00:05:10] Maya: Yes, you can configure routing policies — primary Dedicated with fallback to hosted or to a smaller family of models. We'll capture latency and cost tradeoffs in the proposed design.
[00:05:19] Alex: Good. On legal and data retention, we have contractual constraints for deletion requests and data-subject requests. How does Redwood handle data deletion and audit of deletions?
[00:05:29] Sanjay: We provide deletions APIs and can provide auditable logs showing delete operations. For Private, you control the physical data. For Hosted, we manage deletion and provide certificate of deletion in many enterprise contracts.
[00:05:40] Priya: Could you outline the difference in evidentiary control between Hosted and Private?
[00:05:46] Maya: Hosted: Redwood manages infrastructure, you get SOC2 artifacts and contractual security addenda; logs live with us but we can export. Dedicated: single-tenant pool with stronger isolation, configurable log streams, and dedicated KMS options. Private: you control the infrastructure, keys, and storage — maximal control for compliance.
[00:06:05] Alex: Sounds reasonable. Let's talk about the demo / proof-of-concept next steps. We want to run a benchmark with a sample PHI workload against Dedicated to validate latency and also verify log exports into our SIEM.
[00:06:16] Maya: Perfect. Sanjay will run the benchmark playbook and we'll pair with Jordan to instrument logs. We'll need a short network checklist for VPC peering.
[00:06:24] Jordan: On the checklist, we need CIDR ranges, expected ports, and whether you support PrivateLink or VPN.
[00:06:30] Sanjay: We support AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering, and can provide standard firewall rules. I'll include those in the architecture doc.
[00:06:36] Alex: Any blockers around encryption for transit?
[00:06:39] Sanjay: No blockers; we'll use TLS and optional mTLS.
[00:06:43] [00:06:43] -- brief cross talk --
[00:07:00] Maya: (chuckles) there's a bit of motor noise from someone on the line — no worries.
[00:07:12] Maya: Ok I want to call out a few artifacts we'll send: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 snapshot, SSP, penetration test summary, KMS integration notes, RBAC mapping template, and our onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private.
[00:07:28] Alex: Great. For the SOC2 and SSP, do you have an executive summary we can share with legal?
[00:07:34] Maya: Yes, we'll include a short bulletized executive summary for legal review.
[00:07:40] Priya: On SAML specifics — do you support attribute-based access control or just group mappings?
[00:07:45] Sanjay: We support SAML attribute mapping to roles and attribute-based rules in the Console. We also support SCIM for provisioning so groups can sync automatically.
[00:07:55] Jordan: One nit — when you do continuous batching, is there any added surface for data leakage between tenants?
[00:08:02] Sanjay: No, we maintain logical isolation at the request level. Batching is an execution optimization; we never mix model state across tenants. We'll include a short explanation and diagrams.
[00:08:13] Alex: If we go Private, we need to run your code package in our air-gapped environment for certain workloads; is that something you support?
[00:08:20] Maya: Yes, our Private offering can be deployed on-prem. We have an air-gapped install procedure and we can arrange a stubbed demo for that flow — though that's a heavier lift and usually reserved for higher-tier contracts.
[00:08:33] Priya: Licensing and support SLAs for Private?
[00:08:36] Maya: Private includes a platform fee plus support tiers. We'll share the pricing ranges and SLA options in the follow-up.
[00:08:44] Jordan: For audit logs, how do you sign and verify immutability? We need proof for audits.
[00:08:51] Sanjay: We provide append-only logs, TTL-based retention policies, and can provide cryptographic hash sequencing for high-assurance customers. We'll add that to the architecture doc.
[00:09:02] Alex: Ok great. Anything else on compliance controls?
[00:09:06] Maya: We also support SSO session controls, RBAC, IP allow-listing, and SCIM — we'll map these to your requirements once you send the SSQ.
[00:09:16] Alex: We'll send the questionnaire today.
[00:09:20] Priya: Quick ops question — if we need data deletion for a tenant, and you have backups, what's the deletion workflow?
[00:09:27] Sanjay: We have a governed delete process that records deletion requests; in Private you control backups. For Hosted/Dedicated, we will also provide a deletion certification and remediate backups per the contract timeline.
[00:09:38] Maya: Alright, let's capture next steps: Maya sends SOC2/ISO and security pack; Sanjay sends architecture + VPC checklist; Jordan and Sanjay to schedule benchmark; Alex to provide SSQ and list of auditors.
[00:09:52] Alex: That works.
[00:09:55] Maya: Any blockers on timing? We're aiming to get the deep-dive scheduled next week if possible.
[00:10:00] Jordan: Next week is tight but we can do the benchmark session the week after, ideally 2-hour slot.
[00:10:06] Maya: Great. We'll propose a few times.
[00:10:10] [00:10:10] -- meeting continues with some clarifying Q&A, occasional filler and short pauses --
[00:20:00] Jordan: Question on log formats — do you emit structured JSON logs or text? We prefer structured for SIEM ingestion.
[00:20:06] Sanjay: Structured JSON, with fields for request_id, model, user_id (if provided), latency_ms, tokens, and a hashed session id for privacy.
[00:26:30] Alex: For our legal team, any standard DPA or amendment templates?
[00:26:36] Maya: Yes we have a DPA and a security addendum that covers data processing terms; we'll attach those.
[00:32:15] Priya: Are there regulatory controls for health data (HIPAA) specifically?
[00:32:20] Maya: We don't sign a BAAs lightly; we have customers with PHI using Private deployments and we can discuss controls to meet HIPAA — need to scope specifics.
[00:37:50] Alex: Ok that covers my main questions.
[00:37:55] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and propose times for the deep technical session.
[00:38:02] Jordan: Thanks.
[00:38:05] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:38:08] Maya: I'll send a recap and action items in the next email.
[00:48:00] End of meeting.
